change.switch: "alignment": "identity" in the scene's jbgs_cdgs_options.json (SL/scenes/cdgs/<site>_<prior>, written by scripts/phd/main_fill_v1/cdgs/cdgs_fl_scenes.py); absent = adapter v2 exactly
change.what: the per-view fit (optimize_depth's Adam) is skipped: scale 1, shift 0. The alignment loss is computed in place by jbgs_identity_depth with optimize_depth's own lines: the targets = the view's own observed SfM points (v2 change 1), the same reprojection-error weights and their max-normalisation, the same 0.1 % prune, both depths divided by the site's s (v2 change 2: B0 19.78, B173 주변 23.23, B173만 22.92, R1 28.60), the mean of the weighted squared residuals plus the negative-depth term (0: the prior depth is positive on every target). The depth weight 0.6 exp(-150 L_align) is the official line. The supervision depth and the confidence map are made from the prior render depth in metres as read (0 at no hit). The per-view record (jbgs_alignment.json) keeps scale, shift, shift_m, loss, loss_m2, weight, SfM points used, prior-hit pixel share, and puts the v2 official values of the same view beside them (v2_official, from the scene's jbgs_v2_alignment.json = the previous task's GPU check reading SB/prep/cdgs/check/<unit>/align_views.json).
change.why: the previous task's per-view fit did not separate scale and shift on aerial views whose depths lie within 50-75 m (scale 0.13 or below 0 at some views; order 3 item 1). With a positive scale and a positive fitted depth on every prior-hit pixel the loss's per-view min-max normalisation makes the supervision independent of scale and shift (order 3 item 2), so the fit reaches the result only through the per-view weight and through views whose depth vanishes; the variant keeps the weight's formula and removes the fit.
